title: Moss and the Wobbly Cane
checkpoint: Phase 1 (Introduction) — a wordless story for sharing and talking through together; there are no sounds to decode yet.
note_for_grown_ups: A true-to-life gardening moment: garden canes really do help a wobbly plant stand up straight, especially once two are crossed for extra support.

pages.talk_prompt: This bean plant is leaning right over — what do you think could help it stand up?
pages.illustration: A tall green bean plant leaning sideways in a vegetable patch, Moss the berry-coloured hedgehog noticing beside it.

pages.talk_prompt: Moss has leant one cane against the plant — do you think it will hold?
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog leaning a single brown garden cane against the leaning bean plant, the cane starting to slip.

pages.talk_prompt: The cane has slipped and fallen — how do you think Moss is feeling right now?
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog scratching his head and looking puzzled at the fallen brown cane on the ground beside the still-leaning plant.

pages.talk_prompt: This time Moss has crossed two canes in an X shape — why do you think that might work better?
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog tying two brown garden canes together in a crossed X shape with a loop of green garden twine beside the bean plant.

pages.talk_prompt: The plant is standing tall now — what has changed?
pages.illustration: The green bean plant standing upright, held firmly by two crossed brown canes, Moss the hedgehog checking it.

pages.talk_prompt: Moss looks proud of the vegetable patch now — why do you think plants sometimes need a little help like this?
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog standing back proudly in the vegetable patch, the bean plant now growing straight and tall among other healthy plants.
